accepted.evidence: Dhakal p. 44 explicitly contrasts central-vowel /bəl/ strength with /bal/ light. Turner9161 gives Pali/Prakrit bala strength and Nepali, Maithili and Bihari bal; choose only the strength homonym and preserve the source vowel distinction.

Dhakal p. 46 prints /cʰõṭo/ short and describes its nasal vowel. Turner5071 gives Kumaoni choṭo, Kashmiri ċhoṭu short/small and Nepali choṭo small under *chōṭṭa. The source nasalization remains as printed; the data do not determine a contact-free path.

Dhakal p. 61 prints /naŋ.ṭəi/ naked. Turner6926 gives Maithili nā̃gaṭ, Hindi nãgṭā and Bengali neṅṭā, and explicitly notes deformations in this word family. The Darai -əi ending is preserved without claiming a specific historical suffix.

Dhakal p. 68 prints /dub.ro/ thin. Turner6438 gives Hindi dūbrā and Awadhi dūbar beside Nepali dublo and Bhojpuri dū̆bar under durbala. The r-bearing Darai outcome has regional comparanda, so it is not inferred from Nepali l by itself.

Dhakal p. 67 prints /ga.lu/ cheek. Turner4089 gives Prakrit galla, Old Awadhi gālu, Oriya gāla and Bihari/Maithili gāl. The exact vowel ending is visible in the Old Awadhi comparison; this is the cheek family, not gala throat.

held.reason: Turner10636 places Nepali rāmro good in a -ḍ extension, but Darai ramrə might be a Nepali contact form; the source does not distinguish inheritance and borrowing.
Lakhimpuri baṛkā big is associated with inferred CDIAL11225-2 *vaḍrakk-; the Darai -kə extension needs its own morphological comparison before choosing this node over 11225.
Turner13173 samá has level/flat comparanda but also explicitly labels Pashai sam a Pashto loan; Darai doubled -mm- and its immediate history require local comparison.
